title: Finite lift inside the intersection from a flat quotient-product tensor kernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $E$ an $R$-module, $J$ any set, and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of submodules of $E$. Put $K=\bigcap_{j\in J}N_j$ (with empty intersection $E$), $P=\prod_{j\in J}E/N_j$, and $q:E\to P$, $e\mapsto(e+N_j)_j$; the product has componentwise operations. Write $i_K:K\hookrightarrow E$ for inclusion, and use the tensor products and induced maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $\ker q=K$ and $\ker(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\operatorname{im}(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. Moreover, for every $x\in E\otimes_R M$ satisfying $(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$, there exist a finitely generated submodule $L\subseteq E$ with $L\subseteq K$ and a tensor $z\in L\otimes_R M$ such that $(i_L\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(z)=x$, where $i_L:L\hookrightarrow E$ is inclusion. Here finitely generated means spanned by a finite list of elements; no surjectivity of $q$ and no Mittag-Leffler condition on $M$ are assumed.

proof.text: The map $q$ is $R$-linear because each coordinate $e\mapsto e+N_j$ is linear and the product operations are componentwise. For $e\in E$, $q(e)=0$ if and only if $e+N_j=0$ for every $j$, equivalently $e\in N_j$ for every $j$, equivalently $e\in K$. Thus $\ker q=K=\operatorname{im}i_K$, so $K\xrightarrow{i_K}E\xrightarrow{q}P$ is exact at $E$. This calculation also covers $J=\varnothing$: the condition on all coordinates is vacuous and both $\ker q$ and $K$ are $E$.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), proof, kernel identification after the second displayed map: untensored coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the exact pair $K\xrightarrow{i_K}E\xrightarrow{q}P$ of Step 1, with the given flat module $M$. Its conclusion is exactness of $K\otimes_RM\xrightarrow{i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M}E\otimes_RM\xrightarrow{q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M}P\otimes_RM$ at the middle term. In other words, $\ker(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\operatorname{im}(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. Therefore, for the given $x$ in this kernel, choose $t\in K\otimes_RM$ with $(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(t)=x$. The cited exactness theorem assumes no surjectivity of the second map.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), proof, sentence beginning "Since M is flat the kernel of this arrow"; Tag 00HD (lemma-flat) and Tag 00HB (definition-flat).

proof.text: By generation by pure tensors in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $t=\sum_{a=1}^r u_a\otimes m_a$ with $u_a\in K$ and $m_a\in M$; a scalar coefficient can be absorbed into $m_a$ by bilinearity. Set $e_a=i_K(u_a)$ and $L=\sum_{a=1}^r Re_a\subseteq E$. Every generator lies in $K$, so $L\subseteq K$, and the displayed finite list generates $L$. Let $z=\sum_{a=1}^r\widetilde e_a\otimes m_a\in L\otimes_RM$, where $\widetilde e_a$ is $e_a$ regarded as an element of $L$. The induced-map formula from the same definition gives $(i_L\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(z)=\sum_a e_a\otimes m_a=(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(t)=x$. The empty sum gives $L=0$ and $z=0$ when $t=0$.
